verdict.rationale: The evidence pack contains nothing about Hyper-V, Windows Sandbox, or any native virtualization feature that would let a power-user run a full Windows VM. The only virtualization-adjacent mentions are about WSL (running Linux inside Windows), which is the opposite direction and does not address running Windows itself in a VM for legacy/native apps. Missing for 10: any documentation of Hyper-V/Windows Sandbox, VM licensing terms, or hands-on evidence of running Windows-in-VM for app compatibility.
